title: Pressure induced structural phase transition and magneto-elastic coupling in Eu doped LaCrO$_3$
authors: Asish Kumar Mishra, Mrinmay Sahu, Bhagyashri Giri, Bidisha Mukherjee, Suvashree Mukherjee, Harekrishna Bhunia, Tamalkanti Mukherjee, Sujoy Ghosh, Partha Mitra, Peter Liermann, Goutam Dev Mukherjee
abstract: In this study, we have carried out a detailed high pressure investigation on 5$\%$ Eu doped LaCrO$_3$ (ELCO) using synchrotron X-ray diffraction (XRD), micro Raman spectroscopy, and low-temperature magnetization measurements to correlate the structural and magnetic properties under pressure. The high pressure XRD reveals the orthorhombic to rhombohedral structural phase transition around 10.6 GPa. The high pressure Raman data corroborate this result and indicate that the lattice instabilities associated with the low-frequency soft modes play a crucial role in driving this transition. In addition, a pronounced anomaly in the Raman shift and integrated intensity of several Raman modes is observed around 4.5 GPa. By combining the low-temperature magnetization measurements with the anomalies observed in the XRD and Raman data and by comparing with the similar results in LaCrO$_3$ (LCO), a pressure-induced change in the magnetic ground state to antiferromagnetic ordering is predicted.
summary: This work uses high-pressure XRD, Raman, and magnetization measurements to characterize Eu-doped LaCrO3. It reports a structural phase transition at 10.6 GPa and identifies a critical anomaly at 4.5 GPa. This anomaly strongly suggests the onset of antiferromagnetic ordering, demonstrating significant magneto-elastic coupling in the material.
main_problem: The study investigates how external pressure influences the structural, vibrational, and magnetic properties of Eu-doped LaCrO3 to understand the underlying structure-property correlations.
main_result: The research reveals a pressure-induced structural phase transition from orthorhombic to rhombohedral symmetry around 10.6 GPa, alongside a distinct anomaly at 4.5 GPa suggesting the onset of long-range antiferromagnetic ordering coupled to structural changes.
method: The investigation employs a combination of high-pressure synchrotron X-ray Diffraction (XRD), micro Raman spectroscopy, and low-temperature magnetization measurements.
model_or_system: The physical system is Eu-doped LaCrO3 (ELCO), a perovskite-like oxide material whose properties are studied under extreme pressure conditions.
key_observables: Structural phase transition (Orthorhombic to rhombohedral), lattice parameters, Raman mode shifts and intensities, and the evolution of the Néel temperature ($T_N$).
important_parameters: Pressure (up to 13.5 GPa), doping concentration (5% Eu), and temperature (low-temperature magnetization).
main_assumptions: The analysis combines structural, vibrational, and magnetic measurements to establish a comprehensive link between pressure, structure, and magnetism.
figures_summary: Figures show pressure-dependent XRD patterns indicating peak splitting and structural transitions, volume evolution plots, and Raman spectra tracking mode changes across different pressure regimes.
paper_structure: The paper systematically presents results from XRD to map structural changes, followed by Raman spectroscopy to track vibrational anomalies, and finally integrates magnetization data to pinpoint the magneto-elastic coupling associated with magnetic ordering.
why_interesting: The strong coupling observed between structural transitions (XRD/Raman) and magnetic ordering (Magnetization) provides a rich platform for studying emergent quantum phenomena in correlated oxides, relevant to understanding magnetic ground states under extreme conditions.
